clue.text: Go one better by turning a painter into a rodent

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or go one better than it

indicators.note: turning signals that the little word by just before it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword painter

explanation.surface: Someone tops a rival by magically transforming an artist into a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' applies only to the little word 'by'; RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The capybara is a large South American rodent, the biggest living member of that order.

clue.text: Insist that one is able to dance?

indicators.note: to insist is to say a thing over again for emphasis, so the word comes twice

parts.note: can means is able to

explanation.surface: Asking whether proving you are capable counts as a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone insisting says it twice: 'I can, can!'. 'that one' is link. The cancan is a high-kicking French dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a lively high-kicking stage dance from Paris music halls.

clue.text: Attic poet needing a change of underwear

indicators.note: needing a change of signals that the letters are to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek poet in need of fresh undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a change of underwear' reads as laundry, but 'needing a change of' is the anagram signal for ATTIC POET.
explanation.definitionFit: A petticoat is a woman's slip worn beneath a skirt or dress.

clue.text: Shattered about Archer turning up evidence against English bodyguard

indicators.note: about means going round, so the broken word wraps everything else

parts.note: bust means broken or shattered

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: William Tell was the legendary Swiss archer
proof is evidence that establishes a fact
V for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A broken man, having upended the archery case, finds evidence against an English minder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' turns TELL into LLET; BUST goes 'about' LLET + PROOF + V + E.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective jacket guards the wearer's body against gunfire.

clue.text: Turner is viewable, anyway

indicators.note: viewable either way means the letters read the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A painting by Turner can be looked at any old way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J M W Turner but means anything that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is something that rotates, a thing that spins or revolves.

clue.text: Waggish man has come about the lettuce

indicators.note: has come about pictures one word going round another, so the lettuce sits inside the man

parts.note: Joe is a stock male name for any man
cos is a long-leaved variety of lettuce, the romaine

explanation.surface: A joking fellow has gathered round the salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has come about' is the containment signal, with the man split around the lettuce; cos is the British name for romaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone playful and given to jesting.

clue.text: A position in which one would be very happy?

definitions.text: A position in which one would be very happy?

parts.words: A position in which one would be very happy?
parts.note: read literally, a place perched at the peak of the globe; idiomatically, the phrase for being elated

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for feeling elated literally names the highest point on the planet.

clue.text: Gold piece in circulation

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A gold coin passing from hand to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links; 'circulation' means going round, an orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a circuit around a body, a going round.

clue.text: Tiny tree, could be everlasting

definitions.note: used as a noun, the everlasting means endless time

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A small sapling might live forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges TINY TREE. 'everlasting' is a noun here, as in 'from everlasting to everlasting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both name time without end, infinite duration.

clue.text: Faint, having spent about £50

indicators.note: about means round, so the paid word goes round the money

parts.note: paid means spent, as in money handed over
£ is L for libra, the pound, and 50 is L in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone goes weak after spending around fifty pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The £ sign is L from Latin libra, and 50 is L in Roman numerals, so '£50' gives two Ls; 'having' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid and faint both describe something pale or wan.

clue.text: Place of birth

definitions.meaning: A former province of South Africa, a place on the map
the adjective meaning relating to birth, as in prenatal

explanation.definitionFit: Natal is both a South African region and an adjective for things connected with being born.

clue.text: Easily managed to reverse vehicle on board

indicators.note: to reverse tells us to write the vehicle backwards, as a driver backs up

parts.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle
a table is a board, as in board and lodging or a festive board

explanation.surface: Backing a car onto a trailer bed is straightforward to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' reads like a driving instruction but signals writing the vehicle backwards; 'on' simply joins it to the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractable person or thing is docile and readily controlled.

clue.text: Article about fruit with talk mostly on providing food

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the article wraps the fruit

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a lime is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: mostly means take most of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: talk is taken as itself and then shortened

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about fruit and chatter on catering matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means around here, not concerning; 'mostly' drops the final letter of 'talk'. 'with' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimental means nourishing, supplying nutriment to the body.

clue.text: Affected way to dress?

definitions.meaning: affected in the sense of feigned or assumed, like a false accent
to dress is to don clothes, getting them over the body

explanation.definitionFit: An assumed manner is a feigned one, and getting clothes onto the body is how you dress.

clue.text: Cringe to introduce prince as poet

indicators.note: to introduce means letting another letter into the word, so the prince goes inside

parts.note: to cower is to cringe in fear

explanation.surface: A courtier shrinks back when presenting royalty to a versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to introduce' places P inside COWER. William Cowper (1731-1800) was an English poet and hymn writer.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cowper was an eighteenth-century English verse writer, author of The Task.

clue.text: Dead month to the end of August, without any pleasurable activity

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the month goes round the fun

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
fun is enjoyment or pleasurable activity

indicators.note: the end of picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A lifeless stretch from one month to late August with no enjoyment at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside, in its old sense; 'the end of' takes the last letter of August. 'to' and 'any' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Defunct means no longer living or functioning, extinct.

clue.text: Self-service? Non-stop

definitions.meaning: in a self-service café you fetch your own food, with no staff bringing it to the table
with no pause or delay, continuously

explanation.definitionFit: A self-service place has no staff serving tables, and non-stop travel involves no pauses.

clue.text: Indiscriminate destruction of office space

parts.note: mass is a church office, a service
an acre is a measure of land, an area or space

explanation.surface: Ruthless demolition of a workplace's floor area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' suggests a workplace but means a religious service, the Mass; 'of' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the wholesale slaughter of many people.

clue.text: Gestures to leave cacti on shelf

indicators.note: to leave asks us to let the outer letters fall away, leaving a run of consecutive letters behind

explanation.surface: Someone moves potted cacti off a shelf as a kindly act.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestures are deeds or acts done for show, as in a goodwill gesture.

clue.text: Rites performed on Sabbath by nun

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts one piece on top of the other
performed suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nun carries out religious rites on the holy day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' rearranges RITES into ISTER; 'on' places S above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is a member of a religious order of women.

clue.text: Hong Kong woman not quite in a panic — being brave?

indicators.note: in a panic suggests letters thrown into disorder and rearranged
not quite means drop the last letter of the word

parts.note: woman taken as written before it is shortened

explanation.surface: A woman in Hong Kong almost loses her nerve: is she being courageous?
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims WOMAN to WOMA; 'in a panic' shuffles HK with WOMA. A brave is a Native American warrior, and the Mohawk are an Iroquois nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohawk is a member of an Iroquois people, and brave is the old word for a Native American warrior.

clue.text: Tempestuous girl? And did she remember an inn?

definitions.meaning: the heroine of Shakespeare's The Tempest, daughter of Prospero

definitions.text: And did she remember an inn
definitions.meaning: Belloc's poem Tarantella opens by asking a girl whether she remembers an inn

explanation.walkthrough: The file held 'And Ha she' for 'And did she'. Hilaire Belloc's poem Tarantella begins 'Do you remember an Inn' addressed to a girl by name.
explanation.definitionFit: She is Prospero's daughter in The Tempest and the girl addressed in Belloc's poem Tarantella.

clue.text: Old folks round about getting settled

indicators.note: round means the old folks surround the next piece

parts.note: the aged are old people
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Elderly people gather round and reach an accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is RE, the memo word for concerning, set inside the old folks by 'round'; 'getting' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter agreed upon is settled, decided by consent.

clue.text: A crook needs hands

definitions.meaning: a crook is a shepherd's stick or pole
hands are workers, the people employed somewhere

explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a kind of stick, and the hands of a business are its employees.

clue.text: Sailor with terribly fat behind

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A seaman with a very large backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a noun, a backside, but is the nautical word for towards the stern; 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is the nautical term for towards or at the stern.

clue.text: Pole on all fours, doodling

parts.note: S stands for the south pole
moving on hands and knees is crawling

explanation.surface: A Polish man down on hands and knees is scribbling idly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person but gives S, the south pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodling and scrawling both describe careless, untidy scribbling.

clue.text: Changeable creature turned up outside hospital, back for Christmas

indicators.note: outside means the first piece wraps around the hospital letter

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive, so came
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: back tells us the word for Christmas is read from right to left

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: A fickle animal showed up outside the hospital and returned for the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' means arrived, not reversed: only 'back' signals a reversal, applied to the Christmas word.
explanation.definitionFit: The chameleon is a lizard famous for altering its skin colour.

clue.text: Henri taking a walk by the river

indicators.note: taking a walk suggests the letters wander off and come back rearranged

explanation.surface: A Frenchman strolls along the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a walk' rearranges the letters of HENRI; 'by' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European waterway running from the Alps to the North Sea.

clue.text: Being a bit despondent, it yelps

indicators.note: a bit of a phrase means a run of letters taken from within it

explanation.surface: Feeling a little low, the dog whimpers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb but is the noun for a thing that exists.
explanation.definitionFit: An entity is anything with its own distinct existence, a being.

clue.text: Plastered, egad! Turn the gang out

parts.note: a band is a gang or group of people

indicators.note: turn here means turn over or churn, rearranging the letters of the exclamation

explanation.surface: Drunk and swearing, someone orders the mob to be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' suggests drunkenness but means dressed with a plaster. 'Turn' rearranges EGAD into AGED; 'out' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastered wound has been dressed, covered with sticking plaster or gauze.
